title: Cat without a leash outdoors in Poland
question: Can my cat roam outside without a leash in Poland?
short_answer: There is no national law requiring cats to be on a leash. Cats may roam freely, but the owner is responsible for any damage the cat causes.
conditions: No national law requires cats to be leashed outdoors
However: the owner is legally responsible for damage caused by their cat
Some municipalities (gmina) have local rules restricting free-roaming cats — check locally
Cats in housing estates (osiedle) may be subject to housing cooperative rules
Microchipping your cat makes it easy to identify if lost or caught by animal control
Neutering is strongly encouraged to reduce stray cat populations
exceptions: Stray cats (koty wolno żyjące) are protected under the Animal Protection Act — you cannot harm them
If your cat causes an injury or property damage: you may be held liable
Housing cooperatives may vote to restrict or ban free-roaming cats on their property
penalties: Harming a stray cat: fine up to 1000 PLN or criminal liability under animal protection law
Cat causing damage to neighbours: civil liability of the owner
